dedupe_keys.name: swiss monitoring of exposure to non ionising radiation nis expositionsmonitoring

description: Since 2021 the Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (BAFU) has measured the population's exposure to non-ionising radiation across Switzerland, from sources including broadcast transmitters, mobile base stations and phones, WLAN, high-voltage power lines, railway current at 16.7 Hz, tram ripple currents and the 50 Hz supply. The programme has three measurement modules: walked route measurements with portable exposimeters along predefined routes in city centres, residential and rural areas, stations and inside public transport vehicles; spot measurements in private homes, with scans, short stationary readings in living rooms and 24-hour bedroom monitoring; and permanent stationary stations, running since the end of 2022, that record seasonal and daily variation. Measurements take place in more than 70 municipalities in all cantons; by March 2023 there were 225 outdoor routes, 158 public indoor measurements and 246 public transport surveys. A consortium of three private firms and a public research institute (SwissNIS) does the work under a CHF 1.1 million contract from November 2020. Coverage: Switzerland, 2021 to 2025, with yearly reports for 2021 to 2024. Format and access: annual PDF reports in German with results by frequency band and location type, free. Caveats: no machine-readable data release was found; exposure is below the limit values, so the data describe background levels, not hazards. Simulation uses: environmental effects of broadcast and mobile networks, siting and densification scenarios, and public acceptance of new transmitter sites. Related records: the BAKOM transmitter and mobile site layers give the sources, and the German BNetzA EMF database lists site safety distances.
